messages.message: My rice leaves have brown diamond-shaped spots after three days of rain.

AgroLLM matched your concern to Pest and Disease guidance for Rice.

Immediate steps:
- Remove heavily infected leaves if the infection is still localized.
- Improve air flow and avoid prolonged leaf wetness where possible.
- Monitor whether lesions expand after continuous rain.

This looks urgent or complex enough that a human agricultural adviser should confirm the diagnosis and next action.

Knowledge used:
- Managing rice blast after wet weather - Philippine Rice Disease Field Guide

My pechay leaves started turning pale after I changed fertilizer this week.

AgroLLM matched your concern to Crop Nutrition guidance for Pechay.

Immediate steps:
- Compare recent fertilizer rates with the previous schedule before applying more.
- Inspect whether yellowing starts from older leaves, which may suggest nitrogen deficiency.
- Water evenly and avoid overcorrecting with concentrated fertilizer.

This looks suitable for AI first-level guidance, but you should keep monitoring the crop and escalate if symptoms spread.

knowledge_base.title: Managing rice blast after wet weather
knowledge_base.content: Rice blast often appears as spindle or diamond-shaped lesions and becomes more aggressive after long wet periods and dense crop canopy conditions.
recommendations: Remove heavily infected leaves if the infection is still localized.
Improve air flow and avoid prolonged leaf wetness where possible.
Monitor whether lesions expand after continuous rain.

knowledge_base.title: Early response for corn fall armyworm
knowledge_base.content: Corn fall armyworm pressure often begins with ragged leaves, windowpane feeding, and frass deep in the whorl.
recommendations: Inspect the whorl and leaf funnel for larvae and frass.
Target interventions early while damage is still localized.
Record the percentage of affected plants before deciding the next control step.

knowledge_base.title: Tomato leaf curl linked to whiteflies
knowledge_base.content: Tomato leaf curl combined with whitefly activity can indicate viral pressure that should be contained quickly.
recommendations: Remove severely affected plants if viral symptoms are obvious.
Reduce whitefly pressure around the crop perimeter.
Avoid moving tools from affected plants to healthy blocks without cleaning them.

knowledge_base.title: Soil acidity correction before planting
knowledge_base.content: Acidic soil can restrict nutrient availability and root development. Early correction is usually more effective than late in-season fixes.
recommendations: Test field pH before changing the amendment rate.
Apply lime based on actual pH and soil texture recommendations.
Mix amendments evenly into the root zone when possible.

knowledge_base.title: Nitrogen deficiency in leafy vegetables
knowledge_base.content: Leafy vegetables may show pale older leaves, slower growth, and reduced vigor when nitrogen supply is low or poorly timed.
recommendations: Compare recent fertilizer rates with the previous schedule before applying more.
Inspect whether yellowing starts from older leaves, which may suggest nitrogen deficiency.
Water evenly and avoid overcorrecting with concentrated fertilizer.

knowledge_base.title: Waterlogging response after heavy rain
knowledge_base.content: Standing water can quickly stress roots, reduce oxygen in the soil, and worsen disease pressure if drainage stays blocked.
recommendations: Clear drainage channels first before applying new inputs.
Avoid field traffic while the soil is saturated to limit compaction.
Reassess plant recovery 24 to 48 hours after water recedes.
